newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Rate hike supports Bulgarian lev at close.
newsitem.headline: Rate hike supports Bulgarian lev at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 233.50-234 per dollar, up from 236.80-237 in the morning, as dollar demand fell and supply rose on the interbank market following the central bank's sharp rise in the main interest rate, dealers said.

"The lev closes some 2.0-2.5 levs stronger than morning levels as (foreign currency) demand fell, while supply rose a bit after the central bank said it would hike its main interest rate," a bank dealer said.
In a bid to restore confidence in the slumping lev, the central bank (BNB) on Monday said it raised its central interest rate from 108 percent to 300 percent, effective Tuesday.
The rate rise generated expectations of lev strengthening and final clients, which did not urgently need foreign currency, withdrew from the market in the afternoon, traders said.

Dealers said the record high CIR will probably relieve pressure on the lev in the near term, but the rate rise should be accompanied by other measures to restore depositors' confidence in local banks and the lev.
"If the central bank relies only on the rate hike to stabilise the lev, I think the effect will be short-lived," a third dealer said.
After each of the previous CIR rises from 34 percent in January, the lev has remained stable for no longer than a week or two before resuming its decline, dealers said.
The lev traded near 71 to the dollar at the beginning of the year.
